I hit the tool limit mid-slice, so nothing is packaged yet — but the finding is solid and verified, and it's worth telling you now because it's the one thing that shouldn't ship after a tag.

Where the project actually is
Your last run is green across the board: 996 tests / 0 failed, all 15 §16.3 scenarios passing, ci_local.sh --with-all clearing every gate, tree hygiene passing at 310 authored files. M6's close-out line says "then ci_local.sh --with-all, a drill against the real stack, and the tag." Two items left, and neither is code.

So I read the tree against what a tag makes true — the habit F-39 established. The defect isn't in the tree.

F-42 — the door nobody left open
I queried your published repository through the API (read-only). Verified, not inferred:

has_issues	true
SECURITY.md	404 at root, .github/, and docs/
private vulnerability reporting	disabled
has_wiki	true
description / homepage	null
open issues/PRs so far	0
CONTRIBUTING.md says, in the indicative: "Issues are disabled. There is no bug tracker to file into." They are not, and never have been.

So the repository invites strangers to read the source — which is what the AGPL is for, and which is precisely the population that finds security bugs — and offers them: an Issues tab that is open and that the only relevant document says is closed; no Security tab entry; no private reporting form; no email anywhere in the tree; and a notice that PRs are closed unreviewed. The only working channel is the one the documentation denies exists, and it's public. The first thing anyone does with a join-token forgery is publish it.

The zero open issues is the lucky part — nothing has been lost yet.

Why this is a finding rather than a chore, and a new category for the ledger. F-40 was "the spec was right, the code was right, the transport damaged files." This is: the spec is right, the code is right, and the repository settings disagree with the documents — a layer no document has ever described, no test can reach, and check_tree.sh cannot see. F-38's lesson was a row in the embodiment column should name something executable; this is that lesson applied to the one layer where nothing executable existed.

The generalizable rule, which is the actual repair: a document in this tree states policy, never platform state. "Nothing filed here is triaged" is true wherever it's read and survives someone toggling a checkbox. "Issues are disabled" was true never.

What I completed before the limit
Written and verified:

SECURITY.md (new, root) — private channel, no bounty stated up front, in/out of scope, honest single-maintainer timelines, newest-tag-only support, and a section pointing reporters at §17 first so nobody burns a week re-deriving the ≤120 s replay window or the /register ruling. Plus what a fork operator owes their own guests.
scripts/check_repository.sh (new) — two deliberately unequal halves. Tree half blocking, git+grep only: a policy exists, the three documents cross-reference so none can be rewritten into isolation, and no tracked file asserts a repository setting. Platform half advisory, GitHub API: reports PVR/issues/wiki/description, degrades to a reported SKIP with no token. Advisory because a fork's settings are the fork's business — failing their build over your disclosure preferences would be wrong about the licence. bash -n, shellcheck --severity=warning and --severity=style all clean (I fetched shellcheck 0.11.0 into the sandbox and baselined your existing eight scripts first — clean).
CONTRIBUTING.md (full file) — the false sentence replaced with policy, plus the security carve-out and the reasoning: refusing a feature costs the person who wanted it, who has the source; refusing a report costs an operator's guests, who never chose this software.
docs/REQUIREMENTS.md → rev 4, one new §8 principle + §10 carve-out + revision-history row. Applied by exact-match replacement with a uniqueness assertion per anchor.
Still to write
docs/TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md v1.6 (§16.4 gate, §17 disclosure paragraph, §18 policy-not-platform rule, Appendix A F-42, changelog), docs/DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md F-42 row, docs/OPERATIONS.md (a "somebody reported a vulnerability" runbook + the settings checklist, appended as §16 so nothing renumbers), README.md, scripts/ci_local.sh, .github/workflows/ci.yml (a sixth governance job), docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md as a full file, and _CHANGES.md.
